A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural MJD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, SafeGraph&Advan and S&P 500 forecasting experiments, ablations, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical studies, revises S&P 500 results, and adds experiments using third-party forecasting implementations in Appendix D.3 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The neural MJD parameterization, truncated likelihood, conditional-mean training substitution, regularization, and restarted Euler–Maruyama inference remain unchanged. The added explanation about a shared network and single forward pass clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic MJD trajectories, Texas business spending data, and S&P 500 stock prices. The additional comparison extends evaluation within the existing S&P 500 forecasting task.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds Autoformer, TiDE, N-BEATS, N-HiTS, and TCN to the S&P 500 comparison, substantially broadening the dedicated deterministic forecasting baselines. Existing comparator memberships are retained; NJ-ODE already appears in v1 despite revised wording about its inclusion.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a NeuralForecast evaluation protocol using stated package defaults and the same splits and inputs as the main experiments. Existing splits, preprocessing, horizons, and metric definitions remain unchanged. The new table caption says 'tuned steps,' leaving its precise training configuration ambiguous.

E4.justification: The teacher-forcing and standard Euler–Maruyama ablations, runtime comparison, and synthetic qualitative example are unchanged. No new robustness, sensitivity, error, or mechanism analysis accompanies the additional benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions use ten stochastic inference samples with the same mean, oracle, and likelihood-selected metrics. v2's checklist discusses this existing predictive-variability reporting but adds no seeds, independent training-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises Neural MJD's reported S&P 500 scores, including mean MAE 16.8 to 15.4, MSE 1220 to 1360, and R2 0.938 to 0.953. Table 6 materially changes the comparative picture: under stated common splits and inputs, N-HiTS reports MAE 14.1 and MSE 933, below Neural MJD's mean errors. Other existing result tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–C retain their substance. Equation 10 removes redundant conditioning on S0, already included in C; theorem/lemma reference wording changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same modeling, likelihood-truncation, solver, and performance claims. The broad claim of outperforming existing approaches is not narrowed in response to the additional baseline results.

C2.justification: The introduction newly distinguishes time-varying MJD parameters from the distribution shifts addressed by normalization and adaptation methods, clarifying the intended interpretation of non-stationarity. The limitations concerning smooth or jump-free data are retained unchanged, moving from D.3 to D.4.

D1.justification: The reported code location changes from YuanpeiG/neural-MJD to DSL-Lab/neural-MJD. Appendix D.3 identifies NeuralForecast as the added baselines' implementation source and describes default settings; the checklist adds explicit data-purchasing guidance. Existing hardware and preprocessing disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds DAIN, ST-norm, RevIN, and DDG-DA citations to distinguish distribution-shift approaches from its modeling target, plus references for Autoformer, TiDE, and N-HiTS. The existing related-work discussion and cited works are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Changes include localized explanatory additions, renaming Winner-Takes-All to Best-of-K (Oracle), affiliation and conference wording, an additional experimental subsection, and a NeurIPS checklist. Most prose and the original narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, relabels oracle-metric headers, adjusts captions, and reflows existing material, including placing Tables 2 and 3 together. Figures 1–5 and the algorithm displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added forecasting baselines make the empirical comparison more informative, including evidence unfavorable to Neural MJD, while the terminology and modeling clarifications improve readability. The benefit is limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Table 6 reports stronger mean-error baselines without corresponding qualification of the superiority claims, and its 'tuned steps' caption conflicts with the default-settings description.
